Rashi on Keritot 18a:11:1.hebrew: ר"מ מחייב - משום שחוטי חוץ, אף על גב דאיכא למימר שמא לא אכל חלב ואשם זה חולין הוא, דלא בעי קביעות לאיסור:
Rashi on Keritot 18a:11:1.english: Rabbi Meir deems [him] obligated - On account of [the prohibition of] slaughtering [offerings] outside [the Temple], even though one can say perhaps he did not eat forbidden fat and this guilt offering is non-sacred, for he does not require establishment of the prohibition.

Rashi on Keritot 18a:11:2.hebrew: וחכמים פוטרין - דלא איקבע איסורא, דשמא חולין הוא:
Rashi on Keritot 18a:11:2.english: And the Sages deem [him] exempt - For the prohibition was not established, as perhaps it is non-sacred.

Rashi on Keritot 18a:12:1.hebrew: ואמאי - אצטער דלא אמר לו ר' מאיר היא? הוה ליה למימר אשמעתיה דר' אליעזר היא:
Rashi on Keritot 18a:12:1.english: And why - was [Rav Nachman] distressed that he did not say to him [that] it is Rabbi Meir? He should have said, in accordance with his [earlier] teaching, [that] it is Rabbi Eliezer.

Rashi on Keritot 18a:12:2.hebrew: בשיטת ר' אליעזר אמרה - משום הכי מחייב, דלא בעי קביעות איסור. והאי דלא הוה אמר ליה ר' אליעזר היא, לא איכפת ליה, משום דממילא הוה מצי ידע:
Rashi on Keritot 18a:12:2.english: In accordance with the opinion of Rabbi Eliezer he said it - Therefore he obligates [him], because he does not require an established prohibition. And [as for] this that he did not say to him, "[It] is Rabbi Eliezer," he was not concerned [about it], because he could have known [that] on his own.

Rashi on Keritot 18a:13:1.hebrew: אמר רבא כו' - אף על גב דאמרי לעיל פטור, דבעינן שתי חתיכות, לאו דברי הכל אמרי. דהא ר' אליעזר מחייב, כיון דאמר דמתנדב אדם כו' וליכא למימר חולין לעזרה מייתי — הכא ודאי מיחייב, הואיל ובא לידי ספק:
Rashi on Keritot 18a:13:1.english: Rava said, etc. - Even though they said above [that he is] exempt because we require two pieces, they did not state [this according to] everyone's view. For Rabbi Eliezer obligates [him]: since he says that a person may donate [a provisional guilt offering], etc., and one cannot say [that] he is bringing non-sacred [animals] into the Temple courtyard — here he is certainly obligated, since he has come into a state of uncertainty.

Rashi on Keritot 18a:14:1.hebrew: מתנדב אדם כו' - טעמיה דר' אליעזר בגמרא מפרש בפרק בתרא (לקמן כריתות כה.):
Rashi on Keritot 18a:14:1.english: A person may volunteer, etc. - Rabbi Eliezer's reason is explained in the Gemara in the last chapter (below, Keritot 25a).

Rashi on Keritot 18a:15:1.hebrew: אמר רב אשי - האי דבעינן מקצת איסורא, לרבי אליעזר אליבא דבבא בן בוטא קאמר, דאמר בפרק בתרא (שם) שהיה מביא אשם תלוי בכל יום חוץ ממוצאי יום הכיפורים. אמר: "המעון הזה, אילו מניחים אותי הייתי מביא!" אלא אומרים לי (כו'): "המתן עד שתיכנס לבית הספק" — כלומר: המתן עד למחר, שיש מקצת ספק שמא חטאת היום; אבל מוצאי יום הכיפורים אין לחוש בכך, דהא כיפר עליו יום הכיפורים על ספקו, כדאמרינן בפרק בתרא (שם): חייבי אשמות תלויין שעבר עליהן יום הכיפורים פטורין. ואליבא דהאי בעינן מקצת ספק, כגון חתיכה אחת, אפילו לר' אליעזר. אבל רבנן דפליגי אדר' אליעזר בפרק בתרא (שם), דאמרי אין מביאין אשם תלוי אלא על דבר שזדונו כרת, ואי מייתי הוי מכניס חולין לעזרה — הכא נמי פטרי, דדוקא בעינן כדקרינן "מצוות":
Rashi on Keritot 18a:15:1.english: Rav Ashi said - That which we require a partial prohibition [i.e., a single piece of uncertain status], he is stating [according to] Rabbi Eliezer in accordance with [the opinion of] Bava ben Buta, who said in the last chapter (ibid.) that he would bring a provisional guilt offering every day except the night after Yom Kippur. He said: "By this Temple! If they would let me, I would bring [it], except they say to me (etc.): 'Wait until you enter into a situation of uncertainty.'" That is to say: Wait until the next day, when there is a partial uncertainty that perhaps you sinned today; however, [on] the night after Yom Kippur there is no need to be concerned about this, for Yom Kippur has atoned for his uncertainty, as we say in the last chapter (ibid.): Those obligated [to bring] provisional guilt offerings over whom Yom Kippur has passed are exempt. And according to this [opinion], we require a partial uncertainty — such as one piece — even according to Rabbi Eliezer. However, the Rabbis who disagree with Rabbi Eliezer in the last chapter (ibid.), who say [that] one only brings a provisional guilt offering for something whose intentional [violation incurs] karet, and if he brings [one otherwise] he is bringing unconsecrated [animals] into the Temple courtyard — here too they exempt [him], for we specifically require [an established prohibition of two pieces], as we read mitzvot [in the plural].

Rashi on Keritot 18a:16:1.hebrew: וכן אם אכל כלב - את השנייה או עורב, חייב ישראל, הואיל ובשעה שאכל הוה חתיכה משתי חתיכות:
Rashi on Keritot 18a:16:1.english: And likewise if a dog ate - the second [piece], or a raven [ate it], the Jew is liable, since at the time that he ate, it was a piece from two pieces.

Rashi on Keritot 18a:16:2.english: Exempt - Because there are not two pieces.

Rashi on Keritot 18a:16:3.hebrew: ורבי מחייב - דלא בעי ב' חתיכות:
Rashi on Keritot 18a:16:3.english: And Rabbi deems [him] obligated - For he does not require two pieces.

Rashi on Keritot 18a:17:1.english: And the second [piece] intentionally - That he knew it was uncertain.

Rashi on Keritot 18a:17:2.hebrew: חייב - אשם תלוי אקמייתא, דבשוגג הואי ומשתי חתיכות הואי:
Rashi on Keritot 18a:17:2.english: Liable - [To bring] a provisional guilt offering for the first [piece], as it was [eaten] unwittingly and was from two pieces.

Rashi on Keritot 18a:17:3.english: Exempt - Because at the time of the unwitting [eating], there were not two pieces.

Rashi on Keritot 18a:6:1.english: According to Rabbi Zeira, it is impossible to clarify its prohibition - For both of them have been eaten.

Rashi on Keritot 18a:6:2.english: According to Rav Nachman, a prohibition was established - From the outset, and he is liable.

Tosafot on Keritot 18a:11:1.hebrew: השוחט אשם תלוי בחוץ ר' מאיר מחייב - ואף על גב דר' מאיר קאמר לקמן פרק המביא (כריתות דף כג:): "אם נודע לו ספיקו יצא וירעה בעדר", דהוא יוצא לחולין — הכא מיירי קודם שנודע לו, דעדיין שם אשם עליו:
Tosafot on Keritot 18a:11:1.english: "One who slaughters a provisional guilt offering outside [the Temple], Rabbi Meir deems [him] obligated" - Even though Rabbi Meir says later in the chapter HaMevi (Keritot 23b): "If his doubt became known to him, it goes out and grazes with the flock," [meaning] that it goes out to non-sacred status, here [the baraita] is dealing with [a case] before it became known to him, for the designation of a guilt offering is still upon it.

Tosafot on Keritot 18a:11:2.hebrew: וחכמים פוטרין - לאו היינו חכמים דלקמן דפליגי עליה דרבי מאיר פרק המביא (ג"ז שם), דאמר "ירעה עד שיסתאב וימכר ויפלו דמיו לנדבה", דאם כן הקדש גמור הוא וחייבין עליו בחוץ; אלא חכמים היינו כר' מאיר, ועדיפי מר' מאיר, ופטרי אפילו קודם שנודע לו:
Tosafot on Keritot 18a:11:2.english: And the Sages exempt [him] - These are not the Sages [mentioned] below who disagree with Rabbi Meir in the chapter [entitled] HaMevi (this too is there), who say: "It shall graze until it develops a blemish, and be sold, and its proceeds shall fall to [the fund for] freewill-offerings," for if so, it is completely consecrated and one is liable for [slaughtering] it outside [the Temple]; rather, [these] Sages hold like Rabbi Meir, and go even further than Rabbi Meir, and exempt [him] even before it became known to him.

Tosafot on Keritot 18a:13:1.hebrew: באנו למחלוקת רבי אליעזר וחכמים כו'. מאי איריא כי אכלה? אפי' כי לא אכלה נמי, דהא תנן ר' אליעזר אומר מתנדב כו' - ואם תאמר: מאי פריך? אין הכי נמי מתנדב, אבל הכא הוא מחייב אשם עבור חטאו, וקמ"ל צריך שיביאנו ולא בעינן חתיכה משתי חתיכות! ועוד קשה: אמאי לא פריך ליה לעיל על ההיא דר' אליעזר אמר: כוי — חייבין על חלבו אשם תלוי? ויש לומר דהכי פריך: "מאי איריא כי אכלה כו'". פירוש: על כרחך האי ר' אליעזר דהכא לאו היינו רבי אליעזר דכוי, דאם כן מאי קא משמע לן רב נחמן? אלא לעיל גרס רבי אלעזר והכא גרס ר' אליעזר, דהוא בר פלוגתיה דרבי יהושע, וכן מוכח הסוגיא מטעמים אשר פירשתי. ולכך פריך: הא דאמר דבחתיכה אחת מחייב רבי אליעזר אשם תלוי — מנא לך? הא לא משכחת דרבי אליעזר לא מצריך שתי חתיכות אלא מטעמא דאמר "מתנדב אדם אשם [תלוי] בכל יום", ומשום הכי מייתי אפילו בחתיכה אחת; ואם כן חובה לא הוי, ואם כן אפילו כי לא אכל נמי! ומשני: רבי אליעזר [אליבא] דבבא בן בוטא [קאמר], ובמוצאי יום הכיפורים כדפירש הקונטרס. ואתא לאשמועינן דרבי אליעזר סבר יש אם למסורת, ו"מצות" כתיב. (ואף על גב) דאשכחנא דר' אליעזר אית ליה פרק קמא דקדושין (דף יח:) יש אם למסורת גבי "בבגדו בה", ואם כן ליתני: אכלה — חובה, ד"מצות" כתיב בה; לא אכלה — נדבה; מכל מקום, על כרחך לא אייתי הכא מהאי טעמא דסבר דיש אם למסורת, דאם כן מצי מייתי כמו כן אחריני טובא דסבר דיש אם למסורת. ועוד, אפילו סבר בעלמא דיש אם למסורת, סבירא ליה הכא יש אם למקרא, מטעם שפירשתי לעיל:
Tosafot on Keritot 18a:13:1.english: "We have arrived at the dispute between Rabbi Eliezer and the Rabbis," etc. "Why specifically where he ate it? Even if he did not eat it as well, as we learned in the Mishnah: Rabbi Eliezer says: One may volunteer," etc. - And if you ask: What is [the Gemara] asking? Indeed, he may volunteer [a provisional guilt offering], but here he is obligated [to bring] a guilt offering for his sin, and [Rav] teaches us that he must bring it and we do not require one piece out of two pieces! And furthermore, it is difficult: Why did [the Gemara] not ask him above regarding that [statement] where Rabbi Eliezer said: [Regarding] a koy, one is liable for its forbidden fat [to bring] a provisional guilt offering? And one can say that this is what [the Gemara] is asking: "Why specifically where he ate it," etc. Explanation: Perforce, this Rabbi Eliezer here is not the Rabbi Eliezer of [the case of] the koy, for if so, what is Rav Nachman teaching us? Rather, above [the text] reads "Rabbi Elazar," and here it reads "Rabbi Eliezer," who is the disputant of Rabbi Yehoshua — and so the sugya indicates, for the reasons that I have explained. And therefore [the Gemara] asks: That which [Rav] said, that for a single piece Rabbi Eliezer obligates a provisional guilt offering — from where do you [know] this? You do not find that Rabbi Eliezer does not require two pieces except for the reason that he says, "A person may volunteer a [provisional] guilt offering every day," and because of this he brings [it] even for a single piece; and if so, it is not an obligation, and if so, even if he did not eat [it] as well! And [Rav Ashi] answers: Rabbi Eliezer [spoke in accordance with] Bava ben Buta, and on the night after Yom Kippur, as Rashi explained. And he comes to teach us that Rabbi Eliezer holds that the traditional consonantal spelling is authoritative (yesh em la-masoret), and mitzvot is written. (And even though) we find that Rabbi Eliezer holds in the first chapter of Kiddushin (18b) that the traditional consonantal spelling is authoritative regarding bevigdo bah ("in his dealing deceitfully with her"), and if so, let [Rav] teach: if he ate it, it is an obligation because mitzvot is written in it; if he did not eat it, it is voluntary — nevertheless, perforce [Rav] did not bring [this case] here for this reason that he holds yesh em la-masoret, for if so, he could likewise have brought many other [Sages] who hold yesh em la-masoret. And furthermore, even if he holds in general that yesh em la-masoret, here he holds that the vocalized reading is authoritative (yesh em la-mikra), for the reason that I explained above.
